question: What defines the medicalisation of female genital mutilation?

options.A: Having the procedure done by trained healthcare personnel
options.B: Treating the complications of the procedure in a hospital
options.C: Performing the procedure using modern surgical instruments
options.D: Using local anesthesia during traditional cutting ceremonies

explanation: Medicalisation specifically refers to health workers carrying out the procedure, which falsely legitimizes the practice. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T3#GNS225_U6_T3_h1)

question: Why is the involvement of healthcare workers in FGM a major concern for global health bodies?

options.A: It reduces the effectiveness of local anesthesia during birth
options.B: It leads to a shortage of hospital beds for maternity care
options.C: It creates a false sense of safety and legitimizes abuse
options.D: It drives up the financial cost of traditional ceremonies

explanation: When doctors or nurses perform FGM, communities may view the harmful practice as medically sound and acceptable. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T3#GNS225_U6_T3_h1)

question: What is the primary motivation for families seeking medicalised FGM instead of traditional methods?

options.A: Lower financial costs in government clinics
options.B: Availability of government subsidies for the practice
options.D: Desire for reduced health risks and complications

explanation: Families often turn to clinics believing that trained personnel will prevent severe bleeding and infection. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T3#GNS225_U6_T3_h2)

question: Which belief drives health workers to participate in medicalised FGM?

options.A: It is a legally mandated public health vaccination
options.B: Religious texts explicitly require doctor involvement
options.C: Performing a minor cut prevents worse traditional harm
options.D: The procedure improves future fertility outcomes

explanation: Some misguided practitioners rationalize their actions as a harm-reduction strategy, though evidence shows all forms cause damage. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T3#GNS225_U6_T3_h2)

question: What is Type III FGM, also known as infibulation, characterized by?

options.A: Only piercing the clitoral prepuce with a sterile needle
options.B: Narrowing the vaginal opening by cutting and sealing the labia
options.C: Scraping the vaginal walls to reduce internal sensitivity
options.D: Complete removal of the ovaries and fallopian tubes

explanation: Infibulation involves creating a covering seal over the vagina, which causes severe long-term complications. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T3#GNS225_U6_T3_h3)

question: A nurse assisting in a clinic where a patient undergoes partial removal of the clitoris is witnessing which type of FGM?
explanation: Type I specifically involves the partial or total removal of the clitoris or its prepuce. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T3#GNS225_U6_T3_h3)

question: Which of the following is a frequent long-term complication of FGM?

options.B: Complete immunity to urinary tract infections
options.C: Permanent increase in pelvic muscle strength
options.D: Chronic pelvic pain and recurrent infections

explanation: Scar tissue formation and trapped secretions commonly lead to chronic pain and ongoing infections. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T3#GNS225_U6_T3_h4)

question: Why do women who have undergone FGM face higher risks during childbirth?

options.A: The placenta fails to detach from the uterine wall
options.B: Infants always develop congenital heart defects
options.C: Scar tissue restricts the birth canal and causes obstruction
options.D: Their bodies reject standard intravenous pain medications

explanation: Inflexible scar tissue from the cutting and healing process prevents normal stretching during delivery. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T3#GNS225_U6_T3_h4)

question: What is the official stance of major nursing regulatory bodies regarding medicalised FGM?

options.A: It is classified as professional misconduct and punishable by law
options.B: It is permitted if the patient requests it for cultural reasons
options.C: It is allowed only when performed by registered midwives
options.D: It is acceptable as a minor cosmetic procedure in adults

explanation: Nursing councils view FGM as a severe violation of professional ethics and legal statutes. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T3#GNS225_U6_T3_h5)

question: Why does participation in FGM threaten a nurse's professional career?

options.A: It causes nurses to lose their clinical assessment skills
options.B: It prevents nurses from working in private pharmaceutical companies
options.C: It requires specialized training that standard nursing schools lack
options.D: It violates international ethical codes and leads to license revocation

explanation: Engaging in harmful traditional practices breaches professional oaths and results in disciplinary action. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T3#GNS225_U6_T3_h5)

question: What is a key strategy for community health nurses working to prevent FGM?

options.A: Engaging community leaders and traditional influencers in education
options.B: Isolating families who express interest in the procedure
options.C: Performing symbolic cuts quietly in local health posts
options.D: Waiting for patients to report complications before intervening

explanation: Working with respected community figures helps shift cultural norms and promotes sustainable abandonment of the practice. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T3#GNS225_U6_T3_h6)

question: A community health nurse running an anti-FGM campaign should primarily emphasize which message?

options.A: Only traditional birth attendants are qualified to perform cuts
options.B: Medicalisation does not eliminate the physical and psychological harm
options.C: Clinical cleanliness makes the procedure completely safe
options.D: The government provides financial incentives for uncut girls

explanation: Education must counter the myth that sterile instruments make FGM safe or acceptable. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T3#GNS225_U6_T3_h6)
